headline: Comparative genomics dissects resistance, virulence and lineage evolution in bacteria
label: Bacterial Pathogen Genomic Evolution
summary: Large genome and mobilome datasets now resolve how resistance, virulence and mobile elements shape bacterial pathogen lineages.
synthesis: The dominant thread is comparative genomic characterisation of bacterial pathogens, resolving how resistance and virulence determinants and their mobile carriers are distributed and how lineages evolve. Staphylococcal fosfomycin resistance genes are examined for diversity, evolutionary origin and nomenclature, while time-calibrated cgMLST phylogenetics across more than 30,000 S. aureus genomes places Chinese CC398 as a human-associated MSSA lineage distinct from the global LA-MRSA clade. Genomic evolution of Clostridioides difficile is traced from colonization to infection, and a pan-genomic and methylomic analysis identifies a distinct signature in Vibrio alginolyticus from wild fish. MAP provides an open-source Nextflow pipeline for annotating mobile genetic elements and cargo genes (ARGs, VFs, BGCs) in prokaryotic assemblies. Separately, a preprint applies extremophile-derived integrases to temperature-switchable genome editing.
